method: Every ITEM was re-traced against the current working tree with fresh reads (no memory of earlier runs). Files were read from the tree; vendor/ was read read-only to establish framework semantics (Illuminate\Foundation\Bootstrap\HandleExceptions, vlucas/phpdotenv v5.7.0 EntryParser/Lexer). Two PHP language-semantics probes were executed against the local image dujiaoka-php83-arm64-final (PHP 8.3.15) with `php -r` only - no HTTP request, no container start, no payload against any service. No .env value was read or printed.
environment_notes: MODE=static: no EVID_*_RESPONSE evidence exists, so no finding is claimed as dynamically confirmed. Race findings are code-level confirmed but un-reproduced (anti_hallucination Rule 11: single-shot reasoning is not proof of a race).

The assigned line numbers in ITEMS were generated against an older snapshot. The current tree already contains installer hardening (app/Http/Controllers/Home/HomeController.php:135-158) that changes several of the assumptions in PQ-002; this report traces the code as it exists now and rejects the specific hypotheses that no longer hold.

install.lock is git-ignored (.gitignore:15, .dockerignore:13) and required to exist as a *file or dir* only for the installer gate; Dockerfile:14 and conf/start.sh:28-30 create it unless INSTALL=true, so the shipped container is closed by default and the exposure in PQ-002 is a non-container / lock-loss deployment property.
Isolation level: config/database.php:59 sets 'strict' => true and no explicit isolation level, so MySQL defaults to REPEATABLE READ - the assumption behind both race findings.

findings.title: Anonymous POST /do-install (gated only by the absence of install.lock) rewrites .env, imports/drops the whole schema and resets admin_users id=1 to attacker-chosen credentials
findings.verdict: confirmed-code-path / conditionally-exploitable (requires install.lock to be absent on a reachable instance). The two injection hypotheses attached to this item - array-shaped input reaching str_replace unescaped, and phpdotenv escape reshaping of APP_KEY/DB_*/APP_DEBUG - are REFUTED, see rejected[].
related_locations: routes/common/web.php:37-42 - Route::group(['middleware' => ['install.check']]) { GET install -> HomeController@install; POST do-install -> HomeController@doInstall }
app/Http/Middleware/InstallCheck.php:19-23 - the only gate: if (file_exists($installLock)) redirect(url('/')); else $next($request)
app/Http/Kernel.php:74 - 'install.check' => InstallCheck::class (alias only, no auth/throttle stacked on the group)
app/Http/Middleware/DujiaoBoot.php:24-27 - while install.lock is absent every dujiaoka.boot route redirects to /install, i.e. the site advertises its own installer to any visitor
app/Http/Controllers/Home/HomeController.php:138-145 - CRLF guard over the 11 form fields
app/Http/Controllers/Home/HomeController.php:147-158 - admin username 3-32 [A-Za-z0-9_], password >= 10 chars, app_url FILTER_VALIDATE_URL, admin_path ^/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$
app/Http/Controllers/Home/HomeController.php:194-200 - placeholder substitution + escaping of \\, " and $
app/Http/Controllers/Home/HomeController.php:202-216 - file_put_contents(.env) -> DB::unprepared(install.sql) -> admin_users id=1 update -> file_put_contents(install.lock) (lock written LAST)
database/sql/install.sql:7,54,72,... - install.sql is a full DROP TABLE IF EXISTS / CREATE TABLE script (no IF NOT EXISTS, no migration guard)
database/sql/install.sql:246 - INSERT INTO `admin_users` VALUES (1,'admin',<bcrypt>,'Administrator',...); id=1 is then overwritten by HomeController.php:206-211

.env.example:1-45 - the placeholder set the attacker can address: {title},{app_key},{app_url},{db_host},{db_port},{db_database},{db_username},{db_password},{redis_host},{redis_password},{redis_port},{admin_path}
findings.source: Anonymous HTTP request to POST /do-install. $request->all() (HomeController.php:189) plus $request->input() for db_host/db_port/db_database/db_username/db_password/redis_host/redis_password/redis_port/title/app_url/admin_path/admin_username/admin_password (HomeController.php:135-136, 142, 162-173).
findings.sink: Three chained sinks: (1) file_put_contents($envPath=$base/.env, $envTemp, LOCK_EX) at HomeController.php:202; (2) DB::unprepared(file_get_contents(install.sql)) at HomeController.php:204, which mixes DROP TABLE IF EXISTS with the CREATE/INSERT payload; (3) DB::table('admin_users')->where('id',1)->update(['username'=>$adminUsername,'password'=>bcrypt($adminPassword),...]) at HomeController.php:206-211, followed by file_put_contents(install.lock) at HomeController.php:216.
findings.reachability: Anonymous, no session, no token, no CSRF barrier (a CSRF token is obtainable by simply GETting /install first - resources/views/common/install.blade.php:697-700 - and VerifyCsrfToken only excludes pay/*/notify_url and pay/*/return_url, app/Http/Middleware/VerifyCsrfToken.php:23-26). The whole path hinges on one predicate: file_exists(base_path().'/install.lock') === false (InstallCheck.php:20). Shipped container images are closed because Dockerfile:14 and conf/start.sh:28-30 create the lock unless INSTALL=true, and docker-compose mounts a host-side install.lock (docker-compose.yml:13). Exposure therefore exists on (a) bare/composer/php-fpm deployments that never ran the entrypoint, (b) INSTALL=true left set, (c) a host volume where install.lock was deleted or never persisted - and in case (c) the installer accepts a *second* install against a live database.
findings.preconditions: 1) install.lock absent on a network-reachable instance. 2) The attacker-supplied MySQL and Redis endpoints pass the pre-write probes at HomeController.php:177-182 (DB::purge + select 1 limit 1 + Redis set/get) - an attacker can satisfy this with their own reachable MySQL/Redis, or with the site's real values if the site is already configured. 3) For the data-destruction leg, the target schema is the live one (only meaningful when install.lock was lost from an installed site).
findings.impact: One unauthenticated POST rewrites the application's entire .env (DB, Redis, APP_URL, ADMIN_ROUTE_PREFIX, and APP_KEY - the framework re-encrypts with a fresh key on HomeController.php:191-193), then executes the full DDL script and finally sets admin_users id=1 to attacker-chosen username/bcrypt password. On an uninstalled site this is installer hijack: the first visitor to POST wins the administrator account. On a site whose lock went missing it is total takeover plus data loss, because install.sql:7.. is a DROP TABLE IF EXISTS script - every goods/carmis/orders/coupons/admin_users row is dropped and the seed rows (install.sql:246 default admin, install.sql:484-517 default payment gateways) are re-inserted. The freshly generated APP_KEY also invalidates existing encrypted cookies/sessions.
findings.evidence: EVID_BIZ_FLOW_DESCRIPTION: normal install flow = GET /install -> fill form -> POST /do-install -> write .env -> import database/sql/install.sql -> initialise admin id=1 -> write install.lock (HomeController.php:183-217). EVID_BIZ_BYPASS_POINT: the flow has no ownership/authorisation step at all; the single guard is InstallCheck.php:20 `if (file_exists($installLock))`. EVID_BIZ_STATE_PERSISTENCE: HomeController.php:202 `file_put_contents($envPath, $envTemp, LOCK_EX);`, HomeController.php:204 `DB::unprepared(file_get_contents($installSql));`, HomeController.php:206-211 `$updated = DB::table('admin_users')->where('id', 1)->update([...]); if ($updated !== 1) throw`. The lock is written only afterwards (HomeController.php:216), so a partially-completed takeover leaves the installer reachable. EVID_WRITE_CALLSITE / EVID_WRITE_DESTPATH_RESOLVED / EVID_WRITE_CONTENT_SOURCE: destination is the fixed base_path().'/'.'.env' (HomeController.php:185) - no path traversal - and the content is .env.example with `str_replace('{'.$key.'}', $item, $envTemp)` for every request key (HomeController.php:194-199); only the 12 placeholders present in .env.example are addressable, and {app_key} is overwritten server-side at HomeController.php:191-193. EVID_WRITE_EXEC_ACCESSIBILITY: conf/dujiaoka-nginx.conf:31-33 denies `/.` dotfiles, so the written .env is not directly web-readable - the damage is configuration/authority, not disclosure. EVID_WRITE_UPLOAD_RESPONSE: [Not obtained: MODE=static, no request executed].
findings.non_vuln_analysis: Reasons this could be a false positive: (a) it is a web installer by design, and the tree already hardened it - forced admin_username/admin_password with regex + length checks (HomeController.php:135-158), CRLF rejection, double-quote/backslash/dollar escaping, LOCK_EX writes, and a `$updated !== 1` guard so a failed admin reset aborts before the lock is written; the default admin/admin does not survive. (b) The shipped container closes the route (Dockerfile:14, conf/start.sh:28-30, docker-compose.yml:13) and docs/php83-upgrade-deployment.md:153-156 tells operators to pre-create the lock, so the exposure is not the default deployment. (c) There is no authentication to bypass because the route is meant to be pre-install only. After weighing these, the residual defect is real but conditional: a *single-file predicate* protects an operation that rewrites .env, drops every table and reassigns the super-admin. That is an insufficient control for an unauthenticated remote write primitive, so it is reported rather than rejected - with severity held at high and confidence at 0.62 because the precondition (missing lock) is deployment-dependent and was not exercised.
findings.remediation: 1) Require a one-time install token: write a random token to the image/env or a file readable only from the console (`php artisan install:token`), and require it (hash_equals) on POST /do-install. 2) Restrict the installer to loopback/private peers (`$request->ip()` allow-list) or bind it to a CLI-only command (`php artisan dujiaoka:install`) and delete the HTTP route. 3) Make the installer refuse to run against a non-empty schema (probe for existing tables such as `orders`/`admin_users` and abort) instead of executing a DROP TABLE script. 4) Write install.lock *before* touching .env/schema (or use an exclusive lock/atomic rename) so a crash cannot leave the primitive open. 5) Keep .env writes atomic: write to a temp file in the same directory and rename() over .env, preserving the existing mode (currently the umask decides the mode of the newly created .env). 6) Backfill the hardening into docs/_tests_: assert HTTP 403/redirect for POST /do-install when install.lock exists and assert the route is absent in production builds.

findings.title: Card (carmis) allocation in processAuto is a non-locking read-then-update, so two order completions running concurrently can be handed the same card
findings.verdict: confirmed-code-path / conditionally-exploitable (race not dynamically reproduced; requires two payment notifications to overlap)
related_locations: app/Service/CarmisService.php:29-37 - withGoodsByAmountAndStatusUnsold(): SELECT id,carmi FROM carmis WHERE goods_id=? AND status=1 LIMIT ?  (no FOR UPDATE, no sharedLock)
app/Service/CarmisService.php:49-52 - soldByIDS(): UPDATE carmis SET status=2 WHERE id IN (...) AND is_loop=0  (no `AND status=1`, return value discarded)
app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:509-527 - processAuto(): reads the card rows, writes $order->info = implode(PHP_EOL, $carmisInfo), saves status COMPLETED, then marks the ids sold

app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:392-434 - completedOrder(): DB::beginTransaction() ... reads $order via detailOrderSN (plain SELECT), checks STATUS_WAIT_PAY, delivers, salesVolumeIncr, DB::commit()
app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:433 - salesVolumeIncr() runs for every completion path including STATUS_ABNORMAL and the duplicate path
app/Service/OrderService.php:226-230 - detailOrderSN() = Order::query()->with([...])->where('order_sn',$orderSN)->first() (no lock)

app/Models/Goods.php:70-82 - getInStockAttribute() reports in_stock = count(unsold carmis) for auto-delivery goods, so the pre-order stock check (app/Service/OrderService.php:114) is also a stale-count check
database/sql/install.sql:252-266 - carmis has no order_id and no unique key tying a card to an order; only PRIMARY KEY(id) and KEY idx_goods_id
findings.source: Payment-gateway notification / free-order redirect that reaches OrderProcessService::completedOrder($orderSN, $actualPrice, $tradeNo) (12 call sites: app/Http/Controllers/PayController.php:191, app/Http/Controllers/Pay/YipayController.php:101, app/Http/Controllers/Pay/EpusdtController.php:94, app/Http/Controllers/Pay/TokenPayController.php:95, app/Http/Controllers/Pay/PayjsController.php:73, ...). Attacker controls when and how many notifications are in flight by paying N orders at (almost) the same instant.
findings.sink: Carmis::query()->whereIn('id',$ids)->where('is_loop',0)->update(['status'=>Carmis::STATUS_SOLD]) (app/Service/CarmisService.php:51) combined with the delivery of the plaintext card values into $order->info (app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:519-524).
findings.reachability: Anonymous (gateway callback/signature-verified, or free order at app/Http/Controllers/PayController.php:188-196 where actual_price == 0 auto-completes with trade_no 'FREE-<order_sn>'). No queue, no cron, no lock: the only serialisation is the DB transaction, and the read at CarmisService.php:31-35 is a consistent non-locking snapshot under REPEATABLE READ.
findings.preconditions: 1) Goods with type = AUTOMATIC_DELIVERY and at least one unsold carmis row. 2) At least two pending orders for that goods (two buyers, or one attacker buying twice) whose notifications are processed concurrently. 3) The two requests must overlap inside completedOrder - widened by parallel requests, since there is no throttle on the notify endpoints.
findings.impact: Duplicate delivery of one card to two different orders: card T1 SELECTs ids [10] (unsold), card T2 SELECTs ids [10] (REPEATABLE READ snapshot taken before T1 commits), both write the same secret into their own order and both UPDATE status=2. buyer A and buyer B both receive card 10 while only one card existed - direct stock/financial loss, and the shop's inventory count silently diverges from reality. The same window double-counts sales_volume (OrderProcessService.php:433), sends two 'delivered' emails and fires duplicate webhooks. The identical-order variant (replayed notification) double-delivers to the same buyer and double-increments sales_volume; it is less damaging because the buyer already owns the card.
findings.evidence: EVID_RACE_CRITICAL_SECTION: app/Service/CarmisService.php:31-36 (read `->where('status', Carmis::STATUS_UNSOLD)->take($byAmount)->get()`) then app/Service/CarmisService.php:51 / app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:526 (write `->update(['status' => Carmis::STATUS_SOLD])`) - a read-then-write pair with no lock in between. EVID_RACE_SHARED_RESOURCE: rows of table `carmis` (id=10..) for one goods_id; secondarily the `goods.sales_volume` counter. EVID_RACE_WINDOW_ANALYSIS: `grep -rn 'lockForUpdate|sharedLock|Cache::lock|withoutOverlapping' app/` returns no matches at all, so no row lock, no advisory lock and no unique constraint exists; the window is the whole duration of processAuto (card fetch -> eml/queue dispatch, OrderProcessService.php:512-538), and the UPDATE at CarmisService.php:51 does not even filter on status=1, so it succeeds on rows already sold. The order-status guard at OrderProcessService.php:400 is also a non-locking read (OrderService.php:228), which is why the same-order replay variant is not protected either. EVID_RACE_STATISTICAL_RESULT: [Not obtained: MODE=static, no concurrency test executed - this is why the verdict is confirmed-code-path and not 'confirmed vulnerability' per anti_hallucination Rule 11].
findings.non_vuln_analysis: Reasons this could be a false positive: (a) the seller's gateways usually notify sequentially and the window is short - a single notification stream never observes the bug; (b) the duplicate-trade_no dedupe added at OrderProcessService.php:398-410 makes a replayed identical notification mostly idempotent *after* the first commit, so the replay vector is weak; (c) is_loop=1 cards are deliberately excluded from the sold update (CarmisService.php:51 `where('is_loop', 0)`) and validatorLoopCarmis caps them at quantity 1 (OrderService.php:130-140), so reusable cards are a design feature and cannot be 'oversold' - that part of the item is rejected; (d) MySQL will serialise the two UPDATEs on the same row, which can make the bug invisible in light testing. After weighing: there is genuinely no unique constraint, no affected-rows check and no FOR UPDATE anywhere in the codebase, so two concurrent completions of *different* orders can both consume the same row. Reported as a medium-severity race with un-reproduced status, not as a confirmed exploit.
findings.remediation: 1) Claim cards atomically: `UPDATE carmis SET status=2, updated_at=? WHERE goods_id=? AND status=1 AND is_loop=0 ORDER BY id LIMIT n`, then SELECT the claimed rows back (`WHERE status=2 AND claimed_by_order=...`), and abort when affected-rows != buy_amount. 2) Or select with `->lockForUpdate()` inside the existing transaction (OrderProcessService.php:392) and add `AND status=1` to the update plus an affected-rows assertion. 3) Add an ownership column `carmis.order_id` (nullable, UNIQUE per order+row) so a card can never be attributed to two orders, and make the delivery idempotent on retry. 4) Serialise the per-order flow with `Cache::lock('order:'.$orderSN)->block(...)` or a `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the order row before the STATUS_WAIT_PAY check. 5) Move salesVolumeIncr behind the success branch only.

findings.title: Geetest enforcement on order creation is dead code (a Validator object is used as a boolean), so enabling Geetest protects nothing
findings.verdict: confirmed-code-path / directly-exploitable (the defect is unconditional; exploitation only matters once the operator enables Geetest)
related_locations: app/Service/OrderService.php:80-90 - `if (dujiaoka_config_get('is_open_geetest') == BaseModel::STATUS_OPEN && !Validator::make($request->all(), ['geetest_challenge' => 'geetest'], [...])) { throw ... }`
app/Service/Geetest/GeetestServiceProvider.php:17-38 - Validator::extend('geetest', ...) only *registers* the rule; nothing runs until fails()/passes() is called
app/Http/Controllers/Home/OrderController.php:55-95 - createOrder(): validatorCreateOrder() is the single place the geetest branch lives; no other geetest check exists in the create-order path
app/Admin/Forms/SystemSetting.php:49-50 - is_open_img_code switch defaults to BaseModel::STATUS_CLOSE
app/Admin/Forms/SystemSetting.php:89 - is_open_geetest switch defaults to BaseModel::STATUS_CLOSE
app/Rules/VerifyImg.php:29-34 - the image captcha rule is also a no-op while is_open_img_code is closed

routes/common/web.php:20 - Route::post('create-order','OrderController@createOrder') has no 'throttle' middleware; app/Http/Kernel.php:14-25 global stack contains no throttle; 'throttle' appears only for the 'api' group (app/Http/Kernel.php:38-41)
app/Http/Middleware/DujiaoBoot.php:41-53 - when is_open_geetest is ON the middleware only injects geetest id/key into config and renders the widget; it does not validate anything
findings.source: Anonymous POST /create-order (routes/common/web.php:20). Attacker controls geetest_challenge/geetest_validate/geetest_seccode or simply omits them.
findings.sink: Order creation + coupon redemption + downstream payment redirect: OrderService::validatorCreateOrder() fails to throw -> OrderController.php:63-88 continues -> OrderProcessService::createOrder() (app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:312-366) persists an Order and consumes coupon ret.
findings.reachability: Anonymous, unthrottled POST. The branch at OrderService.php:80-90 is evaluated on every order creation; `!Validator::make(...)` is `!<object>` which is always false, so the `&&` short-circuits and the throw at line 89 is unreachable for every request, with Geetest enabled or not.
findings.preconditions: None for the defect itself. Practical abuse requires the operator to have enabled is_open_geetest (SystemSetting.php:89) - i.e. exactly the operators who believe they are bot-protected.
findings.impact: Two independent consequences. (1) Any anti-bot control the operator enables on the checkout is inert: automated clients can create unlimited orders. (2) Because is_open_img_code also defaults to CLOSE (SystemSetting.php:49-50) and POST /create-order is not throttled, the checkout becomes a free oracle: validatorCoupon() distinguishes '优惠码不存在' (OrderService.php:161) from '次数不足' (OrderService.php:165-167), so coupon codes can be enumerated at request speed; every hit also creates an Order row and an OrderExpired queue job (OrderProcessService.php:362-364), so the orders table and the Redis queue can be flooded (storage/worker DoS). With PQ-011 the enumerated coupon can then be amplified.
findings.evidence: EVID_BIZ_FLOW_DESCRIPTION: normal path = POST /create-order -> OrderController::createOrder (OrderController.php:55) -> OrderService::validatorCreateOrder (OrderService.php:58-91) -> validatorGoods/validatorLoopCarmis/validatorCoupon -> OrderProcessService::createOrder -> redirect to /bill. EVID_BIZ_BYPASS_POINT: OrderService.php:80-90 - the guard is `!Validator::make($request->all(), ['geetest_challenge' => 'geetest'], [...])`. Validator::make returns an Illuminate\Validation\Validator instance (never null/false), and PHP evaluates any object as true, so `!$object === false`; the surrounding condition is therefore always false and `throw new RuleValidationException(__('dujiaoka.prompt.geetest_validate_fail'))` (line 89) is dead. The validator is never assigned, so ->fails() is never called and the registered 'geetest' rule (GeetestServiceProvider.php:17) never executes. EVID_BIZ_STATE_PERSISTENCE: OrderProcessService.php:354 `$order->save();` persists the order regardless; OrderController.php:85 `DB::commit();`. EVID_BIZ_EXPLOIT_RESPONSE: [Not obtained: MODE=static, no request executed].
findings.non_vuln_analysis: Reasons this could be a false positive: (a) Geetest is OFF by default (SystemSetting.php:89), so a default install is not 'bypassed' - it simply has no captcha; (b) the geetest rule itself is fragile (GeetestServiceProvider.php:20-25 destructures array_values(request()->only([...])) so a missing parameter would raise an undefined-index error) which could be read as 'enabling it would 500 anyway', but that path is unreachable precisely because of this bug; (c) other validation still runs (email format, by_amount integer >= 1, payway integer, goods open/stock), so an attacker cannot create malformed orders. It is nonetheless a real defect: the guard cannot ever fire, the intended security control silently does nothing, and there is no compensating rate limit, which is the enabling condition for the abuse listed above. Kept at medium with high confidence because the logic error is deterministic and fully verified from source.
findings.remediation: 1) Fix the condition to consult the validation result: `$gv = Validator::make($request->all(), ['geetest_challenge' => 'geetest'], [...])` then `if (dujiaoka_config_get('is_open_geetest') == BaseModel::STATUS_OPEN && $gv->fails()) { throw ... }` (or use `$validator->after()` / a `Geetest` custom rule inside the main validator). 2) Harden the rule so it cannot fatal: use `$r = request();` and `$r->input('geetest_challenge')` etc. with explicit null checks instead of list-destructuring `array_values(only([...]))`. 3) Add defence in depth: `->middleware('throttle:10,1')` (or a per-IP/per-email limiter) on POST /create-order, and a throttle on the coupon-check path. 4) Do not leak coupon existence: return a single generic message for 'not found' and 'exhausted'. 5) Add a regression test that enables is_open_geetest and asserts order creation is refused without a valid challenge.

findings.title: Coupon redemption is a non-atomic check-then-decrement with no lower bound, and the is_use flag is never enforced, so concurrent order creation can spend more uses than the coupon has
findings.verdict: confirmed-code-path / conditionally-exploitable (race not dynamically reproduced; sequential reuse IS blocked, so only concurrency amplifies)
related_locations: app/Service/OrderService.php:154-171 - validatorCoupon(): non-locking SELECT via withHasGoods(), then `if ($coupon->ret <= 0) throw`
app/Service/CouponService.php:29-37 - withHasGoods(): whereHas goods + where is_open=1 + where coupon=? ; is_use is NOT part of the predicate
app/Service/CouponService.php:42-47 - used(): UPDATE coupons SET is_use=2 WHERE coupon=? (unconditional, global)
app/Service/CouponService.php:58-63 - retDecr(): UPDATE coupons SET ret=ret-1 WHERE coupon=? (no `AND ret > 0`, no affected-rows check)
app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:355-361 - used() + retDecr() run at ORDER CREATION, inside the DB transaction opened by OrderController.php:55, before any payment
app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:268-289 - calculateTheActualPrice(): bcsub(total,coupon).bcsub(...,wholesale), clamped to 0 when <= 0
app/Http/Controllers/PayController.php:188-196 - an order whose actual_price == 0 is auto-completed (trade_no 'FREE-<order_sn>'), i.e. a full-discount coupon yields a delivered card with no payment
app/Jobs/OrderExpired.php:52-60 + app/Jobs/CouponBack.php:44-54 - expiry restores ret via retIncrByID and marks the order coupon_is_back; the restore does NOT reset is_use
database/sql/install.sql:275-291 - coupons.ret is signed INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, so it can go negative; UNIQUE KEY idx_coupon(coupon) exists but nothing guards the ret transition
findings.source: Anonymous POST /create-order with coupon_code=<code> (OrderController.php:55 -> OrderService.php:154 -> withHasGoods).
findings.sink: CouponService::retDecr() -> `Coupon::query()->where('coupon',$coupon)->decrement('ret', 1)` (CouponService.php:60-62) and CouponService::used() -> `->update(['is_use' => Coupon::STATUS_USE])` (CouponService.php:44-46), executed at OrderProcessService.php:356-361.
findings.reachability: Anonymous, unthrottled (see PQ-006). The only gate is `$coupon->ret <= 0` on a plain SELECT (OrderService.php:159-167).
findings.preconditions: 1) A coupon attached to the goods (coupons_goods row) with is_open=1 and ret >= 1. 2) Enough concurrent POST /create-order requests that they all execute validatorCoupon before any of them commits its decrement. 3) For direct financial impact, the coupon discount must be large relative to the goods price so that actual_price becomes 0 or small (then PayController.php:188-196 delivers the card without payment).
findings.impact: N concurrent requests with ret=1 all pass the ret<=0 check and all create discounted orders; ret is decremented to -N+1 (the column is signed INT, install.sql:284) instead of being capped. Each of those orders carries the discount, and any whose actual_price evaluates to 0 is auto-completed with a real card by PayController.php:188-196 - so a single-use freebie coupon can pay out N cards, bounded only by goods stock. Secondary: `is_use` is set to 2 globally on the first use and never consulted by withHasGoods, so the 'used' column reports a state the code ignores; and CouponBack restores ret but leaves is_use=2, so the admin list drifts from reality.
findings.evidence: EVID_RACE_CRITICAL_SECTION: app/Service/OrderService.php:165 `if ($coupon->ret <= 0)` (read) -> app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:358-360 `used()` + `retDecr()` (write) inside one transaction, with nothing making the pair atomic. EVID_RACE_SHARED_RESOURCE: the single `coupons` row identified by UNIQUE KEY idx_coupon (install.sql:288), column `ret`. EVID_RACE_WINDOW_ANALYSIS: the decrement is written as a blind relative decrement (CouponService.php:62 `->decrement('ret', 1)`) without a predicate or an affected-rows assertion, so the guard at OrderService.php:165 is advisory only; `grep -rn 'lockForUpdate|sharedLock' app/` returns nothing. Under MySQL REPEATABLE READ each transaction reads the same snapshot of `ret`, so `UPDATE ... SET ret = ret - 1` is applied by every concurrent transaction and the final value is legitimately negative. EVID_RACE_STATISTICAL_RESULT: [Not obtained: MODE=static, no concurrency test executed]. EVID_BIZ_BYPASS_POINT (the is_use half): app/Service/CouponService.php:29-37 shows the predicate is `whereHas(goods).where('is_open',1).where('coupon',$coupon)->first()` - `is_use` is absent, so the STATUS_USE written at CouponService.php:46 can never block a redemption. EVID_BIZ_STATE_PERSISTENCE: app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:354 `$order->save();` + OrderController.php:85 `DB::commit();`; the discount is persisted in `orders.coupon_discount_price` and `orders.actual_price` (OrderProcessService.php:339,348-352). EVID_BIZ_EXPLOIT_RESPONSE: [Not obtained: MODE=static, no request executed].
findings.non_vuln_analysis: Reasons this could be a false positive: (a) sequential reuse is genuinely blocked - once ret reaches 0 validatorCoupon throws, so a naive loop does not work and the bug is concurrency-only; (b) unpaid orders do NOT permanently burn uses in the intended deployment: OrderExpired.php:52-60 dispatches CouponBack, which restores ret via CouponService::retIncrByID (CouponBack.php:48-52), and conf/supervisord.conf:31-38 runs `php artisan queue:work` so the restore actually happens - that part of the ITEM is rejected (see rejected[]); (c) the coupon must be explicitly attached to the goods by the admin, and the discount is a fixed server-side value (`$this->coupon->discount`, OrderProcessService.php:229-237), so no attacker-controlled price reaches the math; (d) calculateTheActualPrice clamps at 0, so the attacker cannot produce a negative total to credit themselves. What remains is a real, unguarded check-then-decrement whose damage is bounded by concurrency and by the discount configured - hence medium (raised from the item's low) with confidence 0.66 and explicit un-reproduced status, rather than a critical claim.
findings.remediation: 1) Make the spend atomic and bounded: `UPDATE coupons SET ret = ret - 1, is_use = 2 WHERE coupon = ? AND ret > 0` and treat `affected_rows === 0` as 'coupon exhausted' (this single change fixes both the overshoot and the missing lower bound). 2) Move the redemption to the payment-success path, or keep it at order creation but restore it deterministically: an idempotent CouponBack keyed on `orders.coupon_is_back` (with its own unique/atomic update) so retries cannot double-restore, and reset is_use when no live order references the coupon. 3) Either honour is_use in withHasGoods (single-use coupons) or drop the column; do not keep a decorative flag. 4) Make `coupons.ret` UNSIGNED or add a CHECK (ret >= 0) so silent overshoot is impossible. 5) Throttle POST /create-order and return a generic error for 'not found' vs 'exhausted' to remove the enumeration oracle.

rejected.title: Array-shaped input (db_host[]=..., title[]=...) reaches str_replace unescaped and reshapes .env
rejected.reason: Refuted at the first line of the guard. app/Http/Controllers/Home/HomeController.php:142 evaluates `preg_match('/[\r\n]/', (string) $request->input($field))`; casting an array to string raises PHP warning E_WARNING 'Array to string conversion' (verified on PHP 8.3.15: error level 2), and Laravel installs a handler that turns any reported warning into an ErrorException - app/Http/Kernel.php global middleware boots Illuminate\Foundation\Bootstrap\HandleExceptions::bootstrap(), which calls error_reporting(-1) (vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Foundation/Bootstrap/HandleExceptions.php:51) and throws in handleError() (same file, lines 66-74). ErrorException extends Exception, so it is caught by `catch (\Exception $exception)` at HomeController.php:224 and the request returns '安装失败' before file_put_contents at line 202 or DB::unprepared at line 204. So an array never reaches the substitution loop. Even if it did, PHP 8.3 rejects the call outright: `str_replace('{title}', ['x'], $s)` raises TypeError 'Argument #2 ($replace) must be of type string when argument #1 ($search) is a string' (verified on PHP 8.3.15) - a TypeError is an Error, not an Exception, so the request would 500 and the write at line 202 would still never happen. The remaining non-string shapes are harmless: int/float/null are coerced by the non-strict-typed call, and `is_string()` is false for them so no escaping is needed.

rejected.title: CRLF / newline injection through an under-escaped installer field adds new keys to .env (APP_DEBUG=true, DB_HOST=...)
rejected.reason: Refuted. The CRLF guard at HomeController.php:138-145 covers exactly the 11 attacker-addressable fields, and those are the complete set of placeholders in .env.example:1-45 (title, app_url, db_host, db_port, db_database, db_username, db_password, redis_host, redis_password, redis_port, admin_path). The twelfth placeholder, {app_key}, is overwritten server-side at HomeController.php:191-193 with Encrypter::generateKey() and is not attacker-addressable because $postData['app_key'] is assigned after $request->all(). A request key that has no matching `{key}` in the template is a no-op for str_replace, so no new line can be introduced and no existing key can be redefined. No decoding layer (%0a/%0d, JSON unicode escapes) applies to a form body read via $request->input().

rejected.title: phpdotenv double-quote escape handling can be bent to break out of the quoted value and rewrite APP_KEY/DB_*/APP_DEBUG
rejected.reason: Refuted. The escaping at HomeController.php:197 is `str_replace(['\\','"','$'], ['\\\\','\\"','\\$'], $item)`, and because str_replace with array arguments applies each pair sequentially, every backslash in the input is doubled *first*. vlucas/phpdotenv v5.7.0 (composer.lock:7154-7155) resolves escapes only in the DOUBLE_QUOTED_STATE/ESCAPE_SEQUENCE_STATE of vendor/vlucas/phpdotenv/src/Parser/EntryParser.php:262-279, where `\\` collapses to a literal backslash and only `\n`/`\r`/`\t`/`\f`/`\v` become control characters. A user-supplied literal `\n` therefore lands in the file as `\\n` and parses back to the two characters backslash+n instead of a newline; a user-supplied `"` lands as `\\"` (literal backslash + escaped quote) and cannot terminate the quoted value. `$` is escaped for the same reason (variable interpolation). Any value that fails to parse raises InvalidFileException from Parser::parse() rather than yielding attacker-chosen keys. The .env write is therefore shape-safe for the fields that are reachable; the residual PQ-002 risk is the unauthenticated write primitive itself, not .env injection.

rejected.title: Replaying the same payment notification for the same order delivers the card twice to the buyer
rejected.reason: Rejected as an independent finding (it is a symptom of PQ-005, with much lower impact). The card content is written into the same order row (OrderProcessService.php:519-524) and the buyer is the same party, so nothing is leaked or double-sold; the recently added duplicate-notification branch at OrderProcessService.php:398-410 returns success (DB::commit + return $order) when the stored trade_no hash_equals the incoming one after the first commit, which makes an identical replay idempotent. The residual effect - salesVolumeIncr doubling (OrderProcessService.php:433) and duplicated MailSend/ApiHook dispatches - is a data-quality/duplicate-notification issue, not a second vulnerability. The genuinely exploitable variant (two *different* orders receiving one card) is reported under PQ-005.

rejected.title: is_loop=1 reusable cards allow unlimited overselling of the goods
rejected.reason: Rejected as a vulnerability - it is the documented semantics of a 循环卡密. app/Service/CarmisService.php:51 deliberately scopes the sold update with `->where('is_loop', 0)`, and app/Service/OrderService.php:130-140 (validatorLoopCarmis) refuses by_amount > 1 whenever the goods has loop cards, so a loop card is intended to be handed to many orders (e.g. a shared account) one unit at a time. Nothing binds a loop card to an order, so 'the same card goes out twice' is expected behaviour here, not a race. The race reported in PQ-005 concerns status-tracked (is_loop=0) cards.

rejected.title: Abandoned/expired orders permanently burn a coupon's remaining uses because ret is never restored
rejected.reason: Refuted for the intended deployment. app/Jobs/OrderExpired.php:52-60 re-reads the order and, when it is still STATUS_WAIT_PAY, marks it expired (OrderService::expiredOrderSN, OrderService.php:228-231) and dispatches CouponBack; app/Jobs/CouponBack.php:44-54 then calls CouponService::retIncrByID (CouponService.php:75-78) to give the use back. The queue worker is started by the shipped supervisor config (conf/supervisord.conf:31-38 `php /app/artisan queue:work --tries=3`), so the restore runs. Caveat worth recording operationally (not a vulnerability in itself): with QUEUE_CONNECTION=redis (.env.example:36) a non-container deployment that does not run a worker loses the restore *and* the expiry transition - in that degraded mode the ITEM's claim becomes true, but the root cause is the missing worker. The real defect in this area is the non-atomic decrement / unenforced is_use, reported in PQ-011.

rejected.title: calculateTheCouponPrice / calculateTheActualPrice lets the attacker tamper with the payable amount
rejected.reason: Refuted. app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:229-237 returns the coupon's stored `discount` column verbatim (a server-side admin value from the coupons table, install.sql:278), and calculateTheActualPrice (OrderProcessService.php:283-291) uses bcmul/bcsub on goods.actual_price and buy_amount and clamps at 0, so no request parameter reaches the arithmetic and a negative total is impossible. The only attacker-controlled inputs are gid, by_amount, payway and coupon_code, each validated in validatorCreateOrder/validatorGoods (OrderService.php:58-121). No price tampering was found on this path; the coupon *quantity* defect is reported separately in PQ-011.
